Subject: Renewal planning — need flexibility on term & burn profile

Hi Mateo —

We’re planning our FY28 budget and want to lock in Redwood for inference across two teams (Platform + Search). A few asks from procurement: multi-year pricing options (2yr/3yr) with a clear ramp schedule, the ability to true-up usage quarterly, and an option to opt out of auto-renew with a 60‑day notice.

Two practical constraints: our fiscal year ends 31 Oct, and we want the contract term to co-term with our cloud services which renew on 01 Nov. Ideally the term would start 01 Nov/2027. Also, Platform wants the ability to add burst capacity for holiday spikes without renegotiating baseline commits.

Can you propose 2–3 structure options we can take to procurement next week? High level is fine (pricing band, ramp %, true-up cadence, opt‑out clause). If you can include an example invoicing cadence and when credits would apply, that’d be helpful.

Thanks —
Elena

Head of Platform, Crestline.io

Elena —

Appreciate the clarity. I’ve sketched three pragmatic structures below and attached a short proposal PDF with numbers (redwood_proposal_mateo_v1.pdf). High level: all options allow quarterly true-ups, a 60‑day auto‑renew opt-out, and an add-on burst pool purchasable on-demand with a capped overage rate.

Option A — 2yr phased ramp (conservative)
- Term: 24 months starting 2027‑11‑01
- Commit: Year1 baseline = 60% of current run-rate; Year2 = 100% (linear quarter-over-quarter ramp)
- True-up: quarterly; invoice credit applied to next invoice for over-provisioned credits; overage billed monthly at standard overage rate
- Burst: on-demand pool with 20% of Year2 baseline capacity at a +30% overage premium
- Benefit: lower near-term spend; simpler true-up timing

Option B — 3yr stepped discount (balanced growth)
- Term: 36 months starting 2027‑11‑01
- Commit: Year1 = 50% baseline, Year2 = 85% baseline, Year3 = 120% (allows growth)
- Pricing: unit price reduces ~12% in Yr2 and another ~8% in Yr3 relative to Yr1
- True-up: quarterly with a 60‑day cap on retro true‑ups to limit procurement surprises
- Burst: reserved burst window (pre‑purchased credits) + on‑demand option; burst credits priced at a blended rate
- Benefit: predictable blended unit economics and incentive to consolidate usage under Redwood

Option C — Annual auto‑renew with co-terming & convertible credits (aggressive)
- Term: 36 months but with annual billing and a co-terming clause to align start with 2027‑11‑01
- Commit: Annual baseline set each Nov with convertible credits for shortfall/overage transfer between teams
- True-up: quarterly; excess usage credited into a pool to offset future invoices (useful for cross-team variability)
- Opt‑out: 60‑day notice each year
- Benefit: maximum flexibility for distributed teams, good for customers expecting shifting load between Platform and Search

Next steps I propose: 1) You pick 1–2 preferred options; 2) Karthik will tighten pricing bands and prepare a redline-friendly amendment; 3) Sales Ops/Legal prepare a one‑page amendment for procurement review.

I’ve attached the PDF with estimated pricing ranges and an example invoice cadence. Happy to hop on a quick 20‑minute call tomorrow if helpful.

—Mateo
Mateo Alvarez
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference

Elena / team —

Thanks Mateo — adding a bit more color on pricing and the legal/ops constraints we see:

Pricing sketches (banded estimates) — public-facing numbers removed for thread export, but example structure:
- 2yr (Option A): ~X% discount off list, limited to utilization tiers; favorable if Crestline wants lower near-term cash out
- 3yr (Option B): deeper blended discount with annual step-down; we can surface a blended $/token bucket for Yr2/Yr3
- Convertible credits (Option C): requires explicit language around credit expiry and inter-team transferability (we recommend 12–18 month expiry)

Operational notes:
- Co-terming to 01 Nov start: Sales Ops will prepare a prorated invoice for the Nov->Dec partial month if executed before Nov 1; otherwise contract effective 11/01 and first invoice on 11/01
- Burst model: we need to agree on soft/firm capacity buckets and an overage cap (we usually recommend a 2x ceiling to protect both sides)

Lauren — can you prepare a draft amendment (single page) for procurement capturing Option B as the recommended default + Option A as a conservative fallback? Please include the DocuSign placeholder and an SSO/KMS clause for Private deployments (Elena mentioned compliance to procurement).

Elena — happy to be on the call with procurement as needed. If procurement wants more granularity on invoice cadence or GL codes for payments, loop them in and we’ll have Finance Ops fill the fields.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer

Team —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. Procurement reviewed and they prefer Option B (3yr stepped discount) but want the convertible credits to have a 12‑month expiry (rather than 18). They also asked that the burst ceiling be capped at 1.5x Year2 baseline and that any unused burst credits in a year roll into the next year only if the Year2 baseline is met.

Samir (procurement) will pick up legal redlines — he’ll need the single‑page amendment Karthik mentioned and a sample SOW showing how Platform + Search teams will be billed separately under the same contract. We’re ready to move to signature once those two items are in place.

Elena

Head of Platform, Crestline.io
